sections.heading: Attendance
sections.intro: Mandatory. You're allowed to miss 5 classes with no penalty.
items: Miss 6 or 7 classes → lose 1 letter-grade step (e.g. B → B-)
Miss more than 7 → lose 2 letter-grade steps (e.g. B → C+)
Being late or leaving class early/for long stretches lowers participation points
Need more excused absences? You must submit documentation

sections.heading: C code projects — 4 parts each
items: Create a subdirectory "proj<n>" in your course directory
Handwrite the required <starter>.c code in class and submit it
Start your readMe in class (name, student id, use case, design) and keep adding to it — record each work session, what was hard, and cite sources including AI
Build your C code incrementally on the server (gcc or Makefile) with ≥2 saved prior versions of each file

sections.heading: Homework — 3 parts each
items: Create a subdirectory "hw<n>" in your course directory
In class: handwrite + Emacs-type hw<n>.txt on the server
Upload hw<n>.pdf, including photos of handwritten drawings

sections.heading: AI use-case options (for C code projects)
items: Case 1 — none: no AI used; cite any traditional sources or copied code
Case 2 — ahead: AI used only for design before coding, not for the code itself
Case 3 — during: AI used to fix broken code, with START/END markers + prompt around generated sections
Case 4 — entire: AI generated the whole assignment; you must supply handwritten tests/comments proving you understand it and may be called in to demo

sections.heading: AI policy
items: Allowed on C code projects — mark generated sections with START/END and the prompt used, and list the LLM(s) you used in your readMe
NOT allowed for generating homework answers (mostly handwritten/photographed)
Any AI-generated material must be cited (in-text + appendix with full generated text) — uncited use counts as academic dishonesty
Software similarity to other students' code or generated code above 45% (MOSS) earns 0 points

sections.heading: Avoid losing points
items: Use "cp -p" or "scp -p" to copy files — never "mv", which can break permissions
Check files with "ls -la"; Linux is case-sensitive ("HW1" ≠ "hw1")
Keep enough server disk space — check with "du -h"; VSCode alone isn't enough, you must compile/run on the server
Submit required incrementals (dated prior versions) with your project code, matching your readMe's session notes
Late penalty: 1% per hour, down to half the score. Late test arrival = proportionately lower score
